chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Amr ibn Uthman, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The habitual drinker of wine meets Allah when he meets Him like an idol worshipper.'

key_terms.مُدْمِنُ: Habitual drinker / one who is addicted to

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a habitual wine drinker according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the theological gravity of chronic intoxication, equating the habitual drinker's spiritual state to that of a polytheist (mushrik) at the time of death. This comparison underscores that persistent sin can harden the heart to the point of losing monotheistic identity, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of faith for those who neglect ritual prayers due to intoxication. The hadith serves as a critical ethical warning, linking the physical act of drinking to a profound metaphysical transformation in the believer's relationship with Allah.
